title: Resolution model for normalized global site comparison
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-size-convention], with their constant-$\Lambda$ module categories and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes, $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison inverse image, and $N_T=\nu_{T,*}$ for its right adjoint [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact].
Let $U$ be a scheme and $F$ a $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. There exist nonnegative complexes $I,J$, termwise injective and K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and quasi-isomorphisms $i:F[0]\to I$ and $t:A_UI\to J$. For every such pair, $t\circ A_U(i)$ identifies $QJ$ canonically with $A_UF[0]$.
Let $h:I\to N_UJ$ be the chain map adjoint to $t$ and let $w:\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},I)\to\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proet}},J)$ be its evaluation at the final object, using $(N_UJ)(U)=J(U)$. Under the canonical resolution identifications for derived sections, $Qw$ is the global comparison induced by the derived comparison unit and the final-object isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology, lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward]. Thus, for every $q\geq0$ and global degree-$q$ cocycle $z$ of $I$, the specified map $c^q_{U,F}$ sends the global class of $z$ to the global class of $h(z)$ in $J$. Moreover $h(z)=t(A_U(z))$, where $A_U(z)$ means comparison pullback of the terminal section, using the canonical constant-ring unit identification. This holds without requiring $A_U$ to preserve injective objects.
